content.text:
I've built `/work/index.html`: a calendar heatmap with one row per ISO year (2012–2026) and one cell per ISO week. It renders with no errors or warnings.

**The answer: yes, mostly.** Every year has high values in winter and low values in summer. The exceptions:
- **Peak timing moves.** The winter peak falls anywhere from week 46 to week 12.
- **2020–21 breaks the cycle.** After spring 2020 values stay low, and 2020 has the lowest weekly value in the series (196 per 100,000 in week 23). There is almost no winter peak in early 2021.
- **2022 peaks early and highest**, in December.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - rows for ISO years 2012–2026, top to bottom
  R2: done - weeks 1–52/53; week 53 drawn for 2015, 2020, 2026 (computed from the calendar)
  R3: done - YlOrRd sequential scale; legend "ARE consultations per 100,000 population per week"
  R4: done - unreported weeks are white with a faint outline and a "No data" legend entry
  R5: done - week ticks (1, 4, 8, … 52, 53) on x, years on y, both axes titled
  R6: done - title plus one-sentence caption built from the data (trough weeks, peak range, outlier year)
assumptions:
  - Row/column come from the ISO year/week in Kalenderwoche, not from Saison
  - 53-week years: Jan 1 is a Thursday, or a leap year with Jan 1 on a Wednesday
  - Duplicate week rows, if any, are averaged (none expected)
  - Caption statistics use only complete ISO years; a peak range that crosses the new year is reported as "week 46 to week 12"
limitations:
  - 2026-W53 is outlined but empty because it is after the last reported week (2026-W43)
  - Colour starts at 0, so differences between summer weeks are hard to see
  - Tooltip on hover only; the static image shows no exact values
```
